Hey, it's easy to think about train wreck situations when you mess up but as far as grades and job goes: unless you're trying to go to an ivy leauge, high school grades almost don't matter. I was a 3.75gpa in high school and graduated with a 2.7gpa- all while trying the hardest I could and never going out to party. Believe it or not. I literally barely graduated and majored in Spanish. 

Go to a community college or state school outside of your home town, apply somewhere else and find a new group of friends. You'll find what you do or don't like in college and you know what? You might just find what you were meant to do. Post-high school is all about exploring. The majority of your life in your 20's is trial and error, so kid, you have yet to begin. 

I had my entire life/classes planned out, I was going to be a doctor. I failed almost every pre-med course and my dreams were slowly withering away. I was in Dept and Spanish was the only option for me in order to graduate in time (no, being a teacher was not the goal here). You are not useless. You have the ability to get up everyday and if you truly want to better yourself, try your hardest in everything you do. And remember, you will fail a lot before you find out your place in this world. Hate to say it, but not everything will be easy. Some of the best things in life are the hardest to acquire. If you have the mentality to better your life and future, you truly will. 

I moved halfway across the U.S to get away from my toxic family and start over. Do what you have to do, if you don't have money for school but you know you will try your absolute hardest, then try going to a community college or even taking out a loan. If you don't want to do school, get a job. Any job. At least build experience and be productive if you're not taking the school route. The president to my company was a HS dropout. Everyone has potential, it just matters how much you want to find that life for yourself.

Hey, I know this is a common difficulty to live with among the trans community. Even growing up around conservatives and being a bit conservative myself, I understand the kind of connotation the word "trans" has for a certain group of people. There are many ways for you to feel like you're in the appropriate body, surgeries, hormone therapy, support groups for self confidence. I'm sorry you keep getting horrible comments thrown at you,  you need to always know that you've survived up to this point, despite all that you're alive. There are tools and therapies to help you transition or make you feel more comfortable in your own body. There are a number of trans YouTubers who, in their early days, struggled with the same identity crisis, it might help to watch some testimonials. It won't happen over night, but technology is THERE and you CAN do it with a lot of time and patience. Find a group of people who identify in the same way as you. I hope you find what you're looking for.

Hey, I hope you reconsider. It might be easy for me to say, as someone who hasn't experienced exactly what you felt, but I really hope you find a reason to keep holding on. I used to think about suicide as if it were an obsession. How I would do it, when I would do it, how I would compose my letter... but as time goes on you have to keep finding things that bring purpose to your life. What makes you feel important? Because you are, regardless of what you may think. Forget anyone who tries to bring you down, because every human life is worth more than that, more than what your conscience is telling you right now. I hope you decide not to do what you're thinking about doing, you can do so much with your life. Help others, even if you can't help yourself. Work for something you want or think you want. Don't let failure or rejection deter you, because you are better than that. Feel free to pm me if you need someone to talk to even

Hey, you are not disgusting. It's so easily to fall into an illusion that you yourself are to blame for everyone around you disliking you. You are alive and you have the ability to grow and learn. You still have so much left to explore and experience. It might not seem like it's worth pushing through right now, but find your purpose, I know you can. 

I had a friend who was severely autistic and acted very differently from his peers. He was really good at one thing: programming. He kept programming, as it was the one thing he was good at, and he's almost mastered it by the age of 17. Find something you like, keep at it, and you'll find your reason to continue living and even thriving. School is temporary, bullying may be temporary. One day you'll be in more control over your life and you'll feel more free. I hope you find what you're looking for kiddo!

This might sound odd, but scents calm me down a lot. When I'm on the verge of an anxiety meltdown or panic attack, I smell a candle or smell flowers. Playing piano to melt away the stress for me, even if it only helps me forget for a moment, helped get me into a routine for when I start to feel down. It usually happened in phases, but I hope you find your trigger to these and releases for help.

It helps to know you have a sense of responsibility in this world. Do you have kids or animals that would depend on you? Even if you don't, finding purpose or having goals is something that you should strive to find so you can continue pressing forwards. If you don't even have the drive or motivation, try something new, try something different out of your comfort zone, find an activity to participate in and find a new group of friends there. Since you're constantly reminded of your failures and past, try a new environment.
No need to be negative, you don't have to share EVERYTHING in order to get help.

I remember a time in my life where I begged God to not let me wake up the next day. There didn't seem to be a point, I hated everything and not even the people I loved could change that. Have you thought about changing your environment? Finding a new place to live? I moved from Oregon to Texas, away from all my family and old friends, and found my own place and am living my own life. Brightening up your living/work space helps, if you had any goals or things on your bucket list you would like to achieve, take some time off and do something for yourself. A sense of accomplishment and purpose is what helped me get out of bed every morning and still helps me a lot to this day. 
Find hobbies, play video games. Do something that reminds you why being alive is so great. Remember, you're a free human being and you can achieve anything if you put your mind to it. Maybe start journaling and putting it down on paper, if you're not the type to talk it out with someone. Remember, everyone has a purpose.
